Sprouts only ever reach the DMZ. Core never accepts a connection from the DMZ bus: it dials out to farmerbus, and its only inbound path is Envoy's forwarded HTTPS on :5405.

g.text: sprout → Envoy :8443 HTTPS: POST /v1/enroll and POST /v1/refresh. No JWT at Envoy; each route has its own local rate-limit bucket.
sprout → Envoy :8443 WSS/HTTPS: the bus websocket (route "/") and GET /files/ (recipes). jwt_authn checks the alg:EdDSA gateway JWT.
Envoy → farmerbus :5407 WSS: nats-server then validates the sprout's native NATS User JWT (alg ed25519-nkey) against its tenant's Account.
Envoy → farmer :5405 HTTPS (farmer_api, recipe_service): /v1/enroll, /v1/refresh, the JWKS, /files/. The only path from the DMZ into core.
farmer → farmerbus :5406 TLS, dialed outbound from core (farmerbusurl): per-tenant connections, the SYS connection, Account JWT resolver pushes.
saasapi → farmerbus :5406 TLS as a SYS-Account User: internal.tenant.provision / .deprovision (results on internal.tenant.[de]provisioned.<job_id>) and internal.sprout.action.
imas CLI → farmer :5405 (and the bus via farmerbusurl).
BFF → saasapi :8081 /v1/…: shared secret + Keycloak JWT.
Stores are listed by client inside each box rather than
drawn as edges. Everything in core is reached only from
core; NetworkPolicies in both charts enforce the ports.

svg.text: 7 generate NKey + X25519 keypair; sign, with the NKey seed,
imas-enroll-v1, ts, nkey_pub, hostname, sprout_pub, join_token
atomic used_count++; accept nkey under the
Every failure (bad signature, stale timestamp, replay, unknown/revoked/expired/exhausted key, lost redemption race, missing
gateway JWT signer) returns the same 401 {"error":"enrollment_failed"}. A retry with an already-enrolled nkey_pub replays
the existing identity (fresh gateway JWT) without spending another use of the token. Then the sprout dials nats_urls (1→2→3).

svg.text: OpenBao KV v2, one per tenant
Each rotation is a new KV version
Transit has no X25519 DH, hence KV.
key plus former keys in their grace
window. Over the bus, only a submission
sealed under a current key changes it;
a superseded key never comes back.
seal: one copy per tenant key in use (current, + previous in
grace) to the sprout's active sprout_pub
open: tenant keys in use × sprout_pub (active + grace)
Inside: payloadbox.Message{purpose, sprout_id, id, re, iat}. Purpose binds
direction (no reflection); a reply names its request; the sprout drops replays.
cmd.run + cook, both ways, Imas-Payload: box1
X25519 private key on disk, never sent; tenant_x25519_pub pinned. Refuses a
plaintext cmd.run. Re-pins only on a continuity proof that opens under the
pinned key; otherwise the refresher exits (ErrTenantKeyMismatch).
Tenant key rotation: imas keys rotate-tenant-key [--sever]
New KV version. The previous key keeps sealing and opening for
max(boxkeygraceduration, gatewayjwtttl); every retained older version signs a
continuity proof in /v1/refresh and /v1/enroll, and sprouts re-pin on their next refresh.
--sever (suspected exposure): no grace, no proofs; sprouts must re-enroll.
Status: cmd.run and cook are sealed; other boundaries are still plaintext
• Sealed: cmd.run, cook dispatch and nudge (request and reply), box key submissions.
• Plaintext inside TLS: cook step events (job results), test.ping, shell, facts,
cancel, the box key rotate trigger, sprout log shipping. See BUILD-STATUS.md.
• Adopted-legacy tenants share one private key until their first rotation.
• No forward secrecy (accepted in the design): exposure is bounded by
how often the tenant key is rotated.
